title: Local sign geometry and the phase of a complex cutoff
source_hypothesis: Real ordinary order-one f nonpositive only on the support of an exotic compact-base C1, equal to one near the complex cutoff q of order s; 0<=e<=1/4. Proved local derivative and phase bounds have beta=s+(3e-1)/2. Full commutator remainders are uniform under left regularization. The joint operator form CA13, including weight-independent K, remains unproved.
completed_component_scope: Local derivative lemmas, the full complex-symbol commutator identity, conditional operator implication and pointwise sharpness. The related CCE companion proves the joint operator inequality and unrestricted complex propagation.
reviewed_arguments: The completed scope is the local derivative inequality, pointwise phase absorption, full symmetric commutator reduction and sharpness examples. The unrestricted complex-cutoff theorem and joint operator estimate CA13 are explicitly unproved.

A direct visual check of the exact admitted printed page confirms that the prime statement does not repeat the real-valued cutoff assumption. The previous real-cutoff result is retained. Failure of its cancellation is not declared a counterexample to the full theorem.

The cutoff plateau and its actual exotic first derivatives give a uniform sign ball of radius r0*w^(-e) in dimensionless ordinary coordinates. This remains valid for complex C1 and does not impose a fixed conic sign neighborhood.
Taylor with an integral remainder gives the complete finite-radius derivative inequality, including zero value and zero Hessian cases. Both the square-root term and finite-radius term are retained.

Combining that inequality with the ordinary first-derivative bound at g=w^(1-e) yields |df| squared at most C*g*w^(1+e) in normalized coordinates. The physical frequency derivative carries its exact additional w^(-1).
The two Poisson contractions have exactly order beta=s-1/2+3e/2 after extracting sqrt(g). The complex real phase is a{b,f}-b{a,f}, and Young gives its pointwise absorption with remainder order 2beta.

Full mixed products, adjoints and quantization changes isolate the real Weyl phase operator plus a uniform order-2beta error. This is a genuine complete-symbol identity; the complex leading phase is never discarded.

The remaining joint form of B on Qu and the Weyl phase is written as CA13. Its constants and actual regularized domains are specified. The existing measured-data energy and weak-limit proof would complete the theorem if this remaining inequality is proved.

Pointwise positivity is not identified with operator positivity. The generic metric positivity loss would be 2s-1+4e, an e-order excess, and the full BQ product corrections remain an explicit obligation.

A uniformly bounded complex symbol family, with compact time cutoff and actual larger sign cutoffs, proves sharpness. Its derivative quotient is R^(1+e)/2 and its positive combined phase is R^(2beta)/8 for k=1/4. These are pointwise sharpness claims only.

The existing calculus and exact real-cutoff proofs are reused. A possible adaptive square-root route is recorded privately as unproved research, with all missing metric, factorization, localization and constant estimates listed. It supplies no completion claim.
